skill.name: TL_buildViews
skill.description: Build or change a page (view, screen, Ansicht, Seite, Maske) of this application from TopLogic's view elements - tables, forms, master-detail, tabs, charts, navigation entries - or from .view.xml the user gives; see and move through the page the user has open; propose view changes for review and undo them. Load it whenever the user asks for a page, a list, a form, an overview, a change to what a page shows, or points at something on their page.
skill.content:
# Build views You build the pages of THIS running application by configuring TopLogic's view elements. A view is a `.view.xml` file under /WEB-INF/views/; the application renders it with its real data. You never write HTML, CSS or JavaScript, and never invent a tag: `viewElements` lists every tag, `viewElements("tag")` its properties and an example from this application. ## The rules a page is judged by - Plain TopLogic: standard tables, forms over model attributes, the standard New / Delete commands. No explanatory paragraphs, no custom styling. - Master-detail is the backbone: a table of the things (about 40%) beside the form of the selected one. Tabs only for the parts of ONE object; dashboards only for overviews. - Every title and label in English AND German: `<en>Events</en><de>Veranstaltungen</de>`. - Only commands change data - never a table's rows, a channel or a value expression. - A delete asks first (``) and is disabled without a selection. - Show attributes a person reads (a name, a date), never an object without a label. ## How you work 1. If the user points at something ("this table", "this page", "here"), call `whereAmI` - every time, because they may have moved since you last looked. It shows their page: every part with its address and the view file it comes from (`[view ...]`). `act` moves on it for them (open a navigation item, switch a tab, select a row). 2. Read the model (`listTypes`, `listTypeParts`); use real attribute names only. 4-7 columns a user scans a list by; the rest into the form. 3. Changing an existing page: `readView` (outline with addresses + XML), then `editView` with element edits. Never rewrite a whole view for a small change: editView keeps comments and formatting. 4. A new page: write the XML (templates below) with `writeView`, then put it into the navigation with `editView` on the start page (`listViews` and `readView("app.view.xml")`): INSERT_INTO the sidebar a ``. When the start page is an overlay of another module's shell (its nav-items carry `config:position="before" config:reference="..."`), give yours the same two attributes. 5. Every write is checked first: the engine reads the view, compiles its TL-Script against the model and builds the page with the real data. With an error NOTHING is saved and every finding names its line - fix exactly that and save again; at most three rounds, then tell the user what blocks you. XML the user hands you: save it as given, fix only what the check reports. 6. The user's open page shows the change by itself; a change of the start page shows when your answer is finished. Say in one or two sentences what the page shows and where to find it. No XML unless asked. 7. Every write is a change set: `listViewChanges` names them, `revertViewChange` undoes one. When the user wants to look before anything changes, `proposeViewChanges` instead: they review, apply or reject it on the review page (tl-ai-views/view-changes.view.xml). ## Writing view XML - Root `` with `` and one content element. Channels connect elements: a table writes `selection="selectedX"`, a form reads `input="selectedX"`. Declare every channel you name. - `rows` is TL-Script: `all(`module:Type`)`, filtered with `.filter(x -> $x.get(`module:Type#attr`) == ...)`. Model references are backquoted: `module:Type`, `module:Type#attribute`, `module:Enum#VALUE`. - A dialog view has a `` with a `` as its content. - A composition part is never a `<field>`: a single part gets its own `<form>` over a `<derived-channel name="plan" inputs="thing"><expr>t -> $t.get(`module:Type#plan`)</expr></derived-channel>`. Master-detail page (replace module:Type, the channel and the attributes): ```xml <view> <channels> <channel name="selectedThing"/> </channels> <split-panel orientation="horizontal" resizable="true"> <panes> <pane min-size="360" size="40" unit="%"> <panel fill="true"> <title><en>Things</en><de>Dinge</de> DeleteLöschen CancelAbbrechen {"en": "Delete " + $x + "?", "de": $x + " löschen?"}.internationalize()]]> all(`module:Type`)
<en>Thing</en><de>Ding</de>
``` Its create dialog (app/thing-create.view.xml): ```xml <en>New thing</en><de>Neues Ding</de>
``` Answer in the user's language and name pages by the label the user sees.
